# 釋氏稽古略

**ID:** T2037
**Volume:** T49
**Category:** 史傳部類
**Original Category:** 史傳部
**Byline:** 元 覺岸編
**Dynasty:** 元
**Date:** 1354
**Juans:** 4
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T2037

## Contributors
- 覺岸 (A001944)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A late-Yuán Buddhist universal history in four juan, compiled by the Tiāntái-leaning monk [覺岸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A6%BA%E5%B2%B8) (Juéàn) and dated by the author's preface to 1354. It supplies a brief, year-by-year chronological frame from the Pángǔ era through the founding of the Yuán, with Buddhist events inserted into the corresponding years and the standard imperial annals supplied alongside. As a "lüè" 略 ("epitome"), the work is much more compact than the longer Buddhist universal histories ([KR6r0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0012) and [KR6r0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0013)) and was intended as a handbook of essential Buddhist chronology for monks and lay readers. Admitted to the *Sìkù quánshū* under WYG, with the title 釋氏稽古略.

**Abstract**

The author [覺岸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A6%BA%E5%B2%B8), styled Bǎo Zhōu 寶洲, was a Tiāntái monk active in the lower Yangzi at Húzhōu 湖州. The preface is dated 1354 (Zhìzhèng *Jiǎwǔ* 至正甲午). The work is short — only four juan — and is essentially a Buddhist supplement to the standard secular chronological frame: each year is given its imperial annal in a few lines (drawn from the *Tōngjiàn* tradition), followed by relevant Buddhist events in slightly fuller detail.

[覺岸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A6%BA%E5%B2%B8)'s main sources are the *Lìdài sānbǎo jì* ([KR6r0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0011)), the *Fózǔ tǒngjì* ([KR6r0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0012)), the *Fózǔ lìdài tōngzài* ([KR6r0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0013)), various Chán lamp records, and the standard secular histories. He explicitly frames his compilation as a *jīgǔ* 稽古 ("examination of antiquity") in the Confucian tradition: the title deliberately mirrors the Confucian historiographical idiom.

The work was continued by [幻輪](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B9%BB%E8%BC%AA) in [KR6r0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0015) *Shìjiàn jīgǔ lüè xùjí* (1576), which extended the chronicle from the founding of the Yuán through the Míng down to the late sixteenth century.
